Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Martinez (AE, Redwood); Ethan Cole (SE, Redwood); Nina Rao (Head of ML, Verdex); Marcus Hale (Infra Lead, Verdex); Priya Singh (Product)

Summary:
Quick weekly sync to review pilot cost/unit economics and recent tuning changes: batching window adjustments, prefix/KV caching results, and next steps for a staging soak to validate tokens/sec per dollar improvements. Some discussion about latency regressions at 95th pct and tradeoffs for UX-sensitive flows.

Topics Covered:
- Recent run results (24h and 72h aggregate): tokens/sec/$ improvements and where wins came from
- Caching: prefix cache hit rates, effective token savings, impacts on memory/KV consistency
- Batching: larger batch sizes vs tail latency, autoscaling responsiveness
- Cost/latency tradeoffs and when to pick Hosted vs Dedicated for particular endpoints
- Next steps: soak test, updated benchmarks, follow-up security/architecture call

Transcript Body:
[00:00:03] Sophie: hey everyone thanks for hopping on. we wanted to keep this tight — 30 to 45 minutes — cover the numbers from the last 72 hour run and decide on the soak.
[00:00:12] Nina: yep thanks, Sophie. Marcus and I looked at the dashboard earlier. curious to hear about the cache lift you mentioned.
[00:00:20] Ethan: yeah, quick context. we pushed a prefix cache on the long form summarization route on monday night, and we also bumped the batching window from 12ms to 25ms for that route only. initial results show a 28% reduction in tokens emitted per user session and about a 22% improvement in tokens/sec per dollar for that flow.
[00:00:40] Marcus: 22% is great — what about latency? our product team flagged that the 95th shot up during peak.
[00:00:48] Ethan: good callout. p95 did increase ~70ms for that route, from 480ms to 550ms, because of the slightly larger batching window. median was flat. it's an expected tradeoff — more batching aggregates more requests into fewer GPU passes.
[00:01:03] Priya: for user experience that's borderline; we run a real-time preview so anything over 600ms is noticeable. can we tune to keep p95 under 600ms?
[00:01:12] Sophie: absolutely. we think we can tighten the batching window a bit on the high-priority interactive routes and keep the 25ms on throughput-only background jobs. we should identify which endpoints are latency-sensitive — Priya, maybe you can flag them?
[00:01:23] Priya: I'll mark two endpoints: /preview and /inline-assist. the long-form summary can stay throughput optimized.
[00:01:30] Nina: what's the cache hit rate you saw? and is it stable?
[00:01:35] Ethan: overall hit rate for prefix caching on the summary route is ~54% during the peak windows, drops to 47% on low-traffic hours. the effective token savings averaged 18 tokens/request for the route, which compounds given our session length.
[00:01:50] Marcus: how's the KV memory pressure? we don't want OOMs on the private cluster side during spikes.
[00:01:56] Ethan: right now memory usage rose by about 12% on the inference nodes with the caching enabled — within headroom on dedicated staging, but we flagged TTL policies to evict less-used prefixes. we're also recommending a small LRU cap and a slow warmup for the KV to avoid a cold-surge.
[00:02:12] Speaker 4 (Marcus?): ok that makes sense. if we set TTL to 30 minutes and lru cap to 50k keys do you think that will be safe?
[00:02:18] Ethan: yeah that's a good starting point. we'll provide a tuning doc with recommended starting values and observed breakpoints.
[00:02:25] Sophie: on the econ side — tokens/sec per dollar — Ethan built a per-model breakdown. can you summarize the headline?
[00:02:31] Ethan: sure. baseline with no caching and 12ms batching: 1.0 tokens/sec/$ baseline. After caching + 25ms batching on throughput routes: 1.22 tokens/sec/$ for the summary model, while the chat model (low-latency) stayed at ~0.96 because we left batching small. across combined traffic mix we observed net +17% tokens/sec/$ across the pilot.
[00:02:53] Nina: good. when you say tokens/sec/$ is that normalized across the hardware types? we have mixed capacity in our staging cluster — A100 and some older V100s.
[00:03:01] Ethan: yes normalized to effective GPU-hour cost. we weighted by the instance mix you provided. the per-model charts in the sheet show both absolute tokens/sec and normalized per-dollar.
[00:03:10] Priya: are those numbers including the extra memory footprint costs? for private deployments we want TCO to include overhead.
[00:03:17] Sophie: good question — the sheet includes projected memory-backed costs as a small add-on line item; it's conservative but we can tweak it to mirror Verdex's infra costs (Marcus will supply unit costs).
[00:03:26] Marcus: i'll share the exact instance pricing and power costs. also we might want to include ops headcount delta in a later calc.
[00:03:33] Ethan: noted. we can add a sensitivity tab for those inputs.
[00:03:38] Nina: there was a comment earlier about autoscaling — did the larger batches cause overshoot on scale-down?
[00:03:44] Ethan: yes a little. when traffic drops the batching window kept aggregating for a beat, leading to a late-scale-down signal. we're proposing a hybrid policy: fast scale-up, slightly delayed scale-down with an academic decay so we don't oscillate.
[00:03:58] Marcus: so more conservative cool-down is the idea. ok.
[00:04:03] Priya: what about fallbacks — if dedicated capacity hits a slow node, do we have graceful fallback to hosted or to lightweight model?
[00:04:10] Sophie: Redwood runtime supports fallback to a quantized variant or to a hosted burst pool if you've authorized cross-account fallback. for the pilot we've left fallback to hosted disabled but we can enable it for resilience tests.
[00:04:21] Nina: we were hesitant about sending PII to hosted. we need to confirm encryption and KMS flow.
[00:04:27] Sophia: (laughs) Sophie: Sophie here — yes, KMS integration uses customer-managed keys for Private; we'll include the KMS diagram in the security follow up.
[00:04:34] Ethan: also to note, the quantized fallback reduces cost by ~35% but can cause small regressions on output quality on edge cases; we recommend A/B testing the fallback path.
[00:04:46] Marcus: for our test we should run a few hundred requests through the quantized model and compare rouge/faithfulness on the eval set.
[00:04:54] Priya: agreed — add that to the soak criteria.
[00:04:58] Sophie: okay let's talk about the proposed soak. we want Verdex to run a 2-hour soak on staging with the new prefix-caching config, realistic traffic replay, and the hybrid batching policy. Marcus, you ok to run that?
[00:05:09] Marcus: yeah we can schedule it. i want Redwood to provide the exact load profile and the kube manifests/tuning params.
[00:05:16] Sophie: we'll send a link to the load-replay tar and the manifests. Ethan will also attach the recommended TTLs and LRU caps.
[00:05:22] Ethan: on instrumentation please capture p50, p90, p95, p99, GPU utilization, cache hit rate, and token counts per request. also export the raw logs so we can correlate with model outputs.
[00:05:33] Nina: timeline — when can we get the updated docs and projections?
[00:05:37] Sophie: we'll push the revised batching profile and cost projection by EOD 2026-09-04. That gives you time to schedule the soak for the 9th or 10th.
[00:05:45] Nina: great. any open risks we should list now?
[00:05:48] Ethan: one risk is the cache greying effect: if prompts change rapidly, prefix cache hit rate will drop and expected savings evaporate. second is memory pressure on smaller nodes which could force us to lower LRU caps and reduce savings.
[00:06:02] Marcus: for the memory risk we can greenlight a temporary scale-up for the soak so we get realistic failure modes without hitting production pain.
[00:06:09] Sophie: good. i'll note that in the runbook.
[00:06:12] Priya: any competitive concerns? i remember you mentioned OtherCloudAI earlier — do we need to worry about them if we go dedicated?
[00:06:18] Sophie: OtherCloudAI offers an easy managed path but their batching/caching is opaque; our advantage is transparent econ and predictable rollouts. still we should keep an eye on their pricing.
[00:06:28] Nina: sounds fine. Marcus, we'll coordinate on the soak schedule.
[00:06:31] Marcus: will do.
[00:06:34] Speaker 5 (brief silence)
[00:06:40] Sophie: cool, almost done. recap and next steps: Sophie share pricing spreadsheet and load artifacts (due 9/4), Ethan share tokens/sec/$ chart and tuning doc (due 9/7), Marcus run soak and share logs (due 9/10), security follow-up about KMS and SSO (target week 9/14).
[00:06:58] Priya: i'll prepare the UX endpoints list and send it to Sophie today.
[00:07:02] Nina: any final questions?
[00:07:05] Marcus: none from infra.
[00:07:07] Ethan: quick note: we'll also include a short script to produce per-request token breakdowns so you can tie cost to specific flows.
[00:07:14] Sophie: perfect. we'll circle back next week to confirm soak results. thanks everyone.
[00:07:20] Meeting ended.
